title: Burleigh County Jury Summons List Request

communications.subject: North Dakota Open Records Law Request: Burleigh County Jury Summons List Request
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Dakota Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The following materials regarding the compilation and composition of the state’s master jury list:

All reports, databases, spreadsheets, or equivalent materials regarding the jury summons process. Please include the total number of individuals who were summoned, responded, and who were selected to a jury summons.

In the event that there are any fees for obtaining or copying these records, please inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. Should the fees exceed $100, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees as I am requesting the information on behalf of a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and the disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest and will contribute significantly to the public’s understanding of how master jury lists are created. This information is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If possible, please provide the requested documents electronically. However, if this is not feasible, please inform me of the available methods for obtaining these records. Further, if you expect a significant delay in responding to this request, please contact me with information concerning when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption that justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within the timeframe required by the statute.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Angel Carter

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Board of Professional Conduct
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I was seeking copies any and all DEA OPR investigation reports referred to the Board of Professional Conduct for disciplinary recommendations for the years 2015 -2019.  This information and procedures and data is highly publicized as cited in the related hyperlinked news. Produce the reports in a properly redacted format on par with other agencies who regularly make these types of disclosures. 

US Government sponsors bill to cease false narratives / Fake News
https://news.un.org/en/story/2022/04/1115412

DEA RFP Case Management Systems and Failures
Notice ID IST-1234

“Current technical capabilities for information tracking, sharing, and analysis are limited by the design of the current toolset utilized as the primary work enablers for ISTA. These applications were not designed to provide high levels of confidentiality, integrity, or accessibility for those with a need to know; nor where they intended to be the backbone of significant analytical and business processing activities in a high operational tempo (OPTEMPO) office. As workloads increase, the technology becomes a limiting factor for maturing ISTA in a way that would ensure increased capabilities in the mission to detect, deter, and mitigate insider threats.
https://etc.g2xchange.com/statics/doj-rfi-dea-case-management-system/

Review of the Drug 
Enforcement 
Administration’s 
Disciplinary System 
Report Number 
I-2004-002
https://oig.justice.gov/reports/DEA/e0402/final.pdf

DEA agents kept jobs despite serious misconduct
Brad Heath, and Meghan HoyerUSA TODAY

https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2015/09/27/few-dea-agents-fired-misconduct/72805622/

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Fernandes

Best,

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #22-00549-F
communications.communication:
Appeal of DEA FOIA Determination – Case No. 22-00549-F Director Office of Information Policy (OIP) U.S. Department of Justice 441 G Street, NW, 6th Floor Washington, DC 20530 Re: Freedom of Information Act Appeal – Case No. 22-00549-F Dear Director: Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I hereby appeal the DEA’s determination in the above-referenced matter. On August 28, 2025, DEA released 18 pages with extensive redactions under Exemptions 6, 7(C), 7(E), and 7(F). I respectfully submit that the redactions are overly broad and not consistent with FOIA’s foreseeable harm standard, 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A). Based on the context, the records appear to be a type of log file. Many of the withheld entries reflect employee names or identifiers that may no longer be current given the dated nature of the records. The categorical withholding of such information sweeps far more broadly than necessary to protect legitimate privacy or law-enforcement interests. Specifically: 1. Exemption 6 / 7(C) – The assertion of personal privacy is overextended. Where employees are no longer active or the information is purely professional (e.g., log initials, user IDs), disclosure would not constitute an “unwarranted invasion of privacy.” Courts have consistently held that the mere mention of an employee’s name in the course of official duties does not, standing alone, justify nondisclosure. 2. Exemption 7(E) – The withheld information does not appear to reveal techniques or procedures; instead, the formatting suggests routine entries in an administrative log. Withholding every line item under the theory that it might risk circumvention of the law is unsupported and contrary to FOIA’s narrow construction of exemptions. 3. Exemption 7(F) – There has been no showing that release of employee names or log entries could “reasonably be expected to endanger life or physical safety.” This exemption should not be applied in a blanket manner. DEA’s response letter itself acknowledges the requirement to assess foreseeable harm, yet no explanation was provided beyond citation of exemptions. The Supreme Court and D.C.
Circuit have stressed that agencies must demonstrate with specificity how disclosure would cause harm, not simply recite statutory language. Requested Action: - Conduct a de novo review of the 18 pages. - Release all non-exempt and segregable portions of the log-type records. - Reconsider the application of Exemptions 6, 7(C), 7(E), and 7(F) where entries concern routine employee log data or inactive personnel. - Provide a detailed Vaughn index, or equivalent explanation, that identifies the nature of each redaction and the actual harm anticipated from disclosure. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Please do not hesitate to contact me if additional narrowing of scope would assist in prompt processing. Respectfully submitted, William Fernandes An Open Government Project powered by ChatGPT 127052-94319956@requests.muckrock.com

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Request: FBI: ANR Robinson
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act.  I hereby request the following records:

Anything related to ANR Robinson. Mr. Robinson was both a prime minister and a president of Trinidad and Tobago. His death was widely reported in the media:

http://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/apr/13/anr-robinson

Per my understanding of the FBI and their understanding of the FOIA process, I am also requesting that the search include "cross referenced" records, not just main file records for ANR Robinson. I am also requesting any FD-302 forms related to ANR Robinson.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.


Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

communications.subject: FOIA request 1351761 (A.N.R. Robinson)
communications.communication:
Good afternoon Mr. Delaware,

This is in reference to your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request # 1351761-000 for FBI records concerning A.N.R. Robinson.  We are reaching out to you to determine if you are still interested in these records, or, if at this time, you would consider reducing the size of your request from 1,407 pages to under 950 pages, which will move the request to the medium track.  Reducing the size of your request may accelerate the processing and allow for a more timely receipt of the information you seek, as it could potentially place your request into a smaller, faster processing track.  This may also reduce duplication costs, if applicable.  Currently, there is a significant time involved in processing large track cases.  

Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system, and the FBI receives a voluminous amount of requests on a daily, weekly, monthly, and annual basis.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks -simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium (51-949 pages), (large 950-8000 pages), and extra-large (over 8,000 pages) sub-tracks are based upon request size.

Please contact me with regards to this inquiry to let me know if you are still interested in receiving records for this request either in full (the remaining records), or reducing the request to the medium track (not to exceed 949 pages).  If you reduce the size, you can request the additional records with a new FOIA request upon completion of this one.

Thank you for your time and patience.  We hope to hear from you over the next few days so we can discuss these options.

Best regards,

FOIA Negotiation Team
FBI Information Management Division
540-868-1695

Need a status check? Contact FOIPA Questions (foipaquestions@fbi.gov).

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #1351761-000
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Negotiation Team-

Yes, I would like to reduce the size of my request from 1,407 pages to under 950 pages, which will move the request to the medium track. I am hoping to have this request moved into a faster track towards resolution. Please take the steps necessary to move this request to the medium track.

Thank you, I appreciate it.

Best regards,

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: OIG Audits Follow-Up Inbox
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All communications received by the following email address: "OIGAuditsFollowup@oig.dhs.gov" between January 1, 2022 and the present.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

communications.subject: Request Clarification to Rescope 2023-IGAP-00006 / 2022-IGFO-00248
communications.communication:
Andrew Free,

Thank you for your email below regarding your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request, FOIA 2022-IGFO-00248.  We sincerely apologize for the delay in response to your FOIA request and inquiries on it.

On February 1, 2023, via email you requested that we limit your request to the following:

  1.  ICE and CBP detention facility inspections.
  2.  DHS detention or electronic monitoring contractors?
Your request remains too broad in scope. Therefore, we request a rescope of your FOIA and clarification for items 1 and 2 listed above.
Concerning item (1) Please specify the name(s) of the ICE and CBP detention facilities of interest to you and timeframe equal to or less than 2 years.
Concerning item (2) Please provide the names of DHS detention contractor(s) or electronic monitoring contractors which are of interest to you.
Please send rescope/clarification FOIA request to FOIA.OIG@oig.dhs.gov<mailto:FOIA.OIG@oig.dhs.gov> .
Sincerely,
DHS-OIG FOIA Team

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #FOIA 2022-IGFO-00248
communications.communication:
Good afternoon, 

I'm appealing the agency's (untimely) determination that my request is "too broad" in scope, as it has no basis in law or fact.

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #FOIA 2022-IGFO-00248
communications.communication:
Good morning, 

I have appealed your baseless "too broad" determination to go ahead and get this case ready for litigation. If you wish to avoid that outcome, you can further narrow my request as follows: 

(1) Item 1 - You may limit your search to only include ICE facilities, and you may further limit it to include communications from January 1, 2022 - January 1, 2025. Had you timely responded and produced records, your proposed search period of two years would not be necessary. You failure to abide by your obligations under FOIA is not grounds for a determination that my request is now too broad. 

(2) Item 2 - You may limit your search for DHS detention contractors to GEO, CoreCivic, LaSalle, MTC, Akima, and Immigration Centers of America, and you may limit your search for electronic monitoring emails to BI / GEO. 

Thank you, 

Andrew Free

communications.subject: ICE FOIA 2026-ICFO-14329
communications.communication:
01/28/2026 

Andrew Free 
263 Huntington Ave 
Boston, Massachusetts 02115 

RE:	ICE FOIA Case Number 2026-ICFO-14329 
Department of Homeland Security FOIA Case No. 2022-IGFO-00248 
 
Dear Requester: 

This acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the Department of Homeland Security, dated 7/29/2022, seeking records pertaining to "all communications received by the following email address: "OIGAuditsFollowup@oig.dhs.gov" between January 1, 2022 and the present". 

While processing your request, the Department of Homeland Security located records that fall under the purview of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).  Accordingly, your request was referred to this office for processing and direct response to you.  Your request was received in this office on 1/28/2026. 

Due to the increasing number of FOIA requests received by this office, we may encounter some delay in processing your request.  Per §5.5(a) of the DHS FOIA regulations, 6 C.F.R. Part 5, ICE processes FOIA requests according to their order of receipt.  Although ICE’s goal is to respond within 20 business days of receipt of your request, the FOIA does permit a 10-day extension of this time period.  As the subject matter of your request is of substantial interest to two or more components of this Department or of substantial interest to another agency, we will need to consult with those entities before we issue a final response.  Due to these unusual circumstances, ICE will invoke a 10-day extension for your request, as allowed by Title 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). We will make every effort to comply with your request in a timely manner. 

We will construe the submission of your request as an agreement to pay up to $25.00. You will be contacted before any further fees are accrued. 

If you have any questions please contact FOIA Public Liaison, Daniel Edgington at 500 12th Street, SW, Washington DC 20536 or (866) 633-1182.  Additionally, you have a right to seek dispute resolution services from the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) which mediates disputes between FOIA requesters and Federal agencies as a non-exclusive alternative to litigation.  If you are requesting access to your own records (which is considered a Privacy Act request), you should know that OGIS does not have the authority to handle requests made under the Privacy Act of 1974.  You may contact OGIS as follows:  Office of Government Information Services, National Archives and Records Administration, 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001, e-mail at ogis@nara.gov; telephone at 202-741-5770; toll free at 1-877-684-6448. 

Your request has been assigned reference number 2026-ICFO-14329. Please use this number in future correspondence. 

Sincerely, 

ICE FOIA Office 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement 
Freedom of Information Act Office 
500 12th Street, S.W., Stop 5009 
Washington, D.C. 20536-5009

This letter is in response to your status inquiry regarding your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), in which you requested: records regarding all communications received by the following email address: "OIGAuditsFollowup@oig.dhs.gov" between January 1, 2022 and the present..

We currently estimate that processing of your request will be completed within the next 3 to 6 months. Please note that this is an estimate and may be adjusted if circumstances change. 

ICE FOIA processes requests in the order they are received, on a first-in, first-out basis. We apologize for the delay in the processing of your request. Please be assured that a processor in our office will respond to your request as expeditiously as possible. We appreciate your patience as we proceed with your request. 

If you have any questions, you may contact the ICE FOIA Public Liaison at ICEFOIAPublicLiaison@ice.dhs.gov or (202) 732-2159. Your request has been assigned reference number 2026-ICFO-14329. Please include this number in any future correspondence regarding your request. 

Sincerely, 

Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Office

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: David Joel Horowitz (January 10, 1939 – April 29, 2025)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, or generated as a result of investigation or inquiry into FrontPage Magazine editor David Joel Horowitz (January 10, 1939 – April 29, 2025). His death is widely-known and widely reported; as such, privacy concerns under FOIA Exemptions 6 and 7 are voided, as are any concerns under the Privacy Act. For example, you may find a Fox News report on his death at the following link: https://www.foxnews.com/media/conservative-commentator-david-horowitz-dies-86

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records of both HQ and all field offices for all relevant names, agencies, organizations, companies and events including but not limited to those cited in the previous paragraphs and/or links as well as a cross-reference with the Southern Poverty Law Center to include any information provided by the SPLC. My request includes but is not limited to 137, 157, 176, 177, 183, 184, 188, and 214 files. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

title: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (Culver City Police Department)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: South Bay Regional Police Consortium (LA Area) - LexisNexis Data Sharing with Federal LE (Culver City Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

We are working on an article focused on California police departments sharing local data with federal authorities, including ICE via LexisNexis. We identified your agency as part of a South Bay Regional Police Consortium that contracted with LexisNexis for AVCC in or around 2020. This request focuses on data your agency shares with LexisNexis, and interfaces that exist with your agency's RMS/CAD/JMS and LexisNexis's systems, including Accurint, Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC), CommunityCrimeMap.com, or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx)

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with LexisNexis and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]
4) Occasionally we have found consortiums who have negotiated to only share local data with other consortium members, not the 2,400 AVCC federal and local LE subscribers. If you have documentation that your data is only shared locally, please share it. Otherwise you may state there are no responsive documents to item 4. 

We welcome (but do not expect or request) any comments you have about the sharing of local police data with federal authorities via LexisNexis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: SFPD Flock Network Searches
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of August 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
The report should include data logged from the period of August 1, 2025, to the date this request is processed. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

Flock has multiple export options, including the ability to redact or hide certain pieces of data. I am requesting a typical audit export - which should include Org Name, Total Networks Searched, Search Time, Search Reason, Offense Type (if still available, may be associated with older audits), and Text Prompt fields.

These exports should only take several minutes to complete, as I am not requesting officer information, license plate query data, or any other PII. Flock pre-built these audit export functions. If you have any questions please don't hesitate to reach out. 

Best,
Shawn

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: RE: California Public Records Act Request #P266456-072826
communications.communication:
Dear Lt. Polovina,

I'm writing to appeal the redactions applied to the Flock Organization Audit and Network Audit records SFPD has begun producing in response to my request P266456-072826, 7/28/26. This is a rolling production, so this appeal covers everything already sent and everything still to come.

The overwhelming majority of rows reviewed so far includes redactions on five fields: user name, search reason, case number, license plate, and filters. I'm not appealing the name or license plate redactions, those are personal and/or sensitive and I support your need to redact that info. But the blanket redaction of search reason and case number isn't consistent with what I asked for or with a lawful exemption.

My original request specifically named "Search Reason" as a field to produce. Neither reason nor case number identifies a member of the public, and neither is exempt investigative work product; the existence of the search itself was already produced, so SFPD isn't treating the search as confidential, only the stated justification for it.

Under Government Code section 7922.000, SFPD has to justify any withholding with a specific exemption for each redacted field, not a standing practice applied to the export. Under section 7922.525, any reasonably segregable non-exempt information has to be disclosed even when a record contains some exempt material. I've received this same Flock export from more than a dozen other California agencies. None of them redact search reason or case number. If SFPD believes a specific exemption applies here, I'd like to know which one and why it doesn't apply to what comparable agencies in the state is releasing.

To resolve this without further escalation, I'm asking SFPD to:

1. Reissue the records already sent with search reason and case number unredacted.
2. Apply the same standard to the rest of this rolling production going forward.
3. If a specific field is still withheld, cite the applicable Government Code exemption for that field, in writing, per section 7922.000. (only for Reason or Case# if you choose to keep any cells in these columns redacted - all other redactions are good as is - I'm not asking for additional work/justification for those) 

Please provide a substantive response within 15 business days. If the Reason and Case Number redactions stand without a cited legal basis, I reserve the right to file a complaint with the Sunshine Ordinance Task Force and look at a writ of mandate under section 7923.000. I have received millions of rows of data from other agencies, all with the Reason column available for review. I appreciate SFPD's dedication to transparency and hope we can find a reasonable compromise and resolve this redaction issue. 

Thank you,
Shawn Segal

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Skokie Flock ALPR Emails 9-2026
communications.communication:
RE: Skokie Flock ALPR Emails 9-2026

To the FOIA Officer of Skokie Police Department,

This request is made under Illinois Freedom of Information Act. for the following records:

All emails and other written electronic correspondence sent to, received by, or copied ("cc'd" or "bcc'd") to any member of the Village of Skokie Board of Trustees (the Village President and all sitting Trustees, including Trustee Alison Pure Slovin) or to Village Manager John Lockerby, from January 1, 2026 through the date this request is processed, that reference, discuss, or relate to either of the following: "Flock" or "ALPR". Include any attachments to those emails.

For each responsive record, include the sender, all recipients (to/cc/bcc), date, and subject line in addition to the message body, so that correspondence can be attributed to the individual Trustee or the Village Manager who sent or received it. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Fee estimates, if any apply, are requested in advance of fulfillment. Electronic delivery is the preferred method of receipt.

A response is anticipated within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

JB_𝗟𝗨𝗖𝗬 𝝦𝝙𝝘𝗦𝝝𝝥𝗦 𝗟𝝙𝝗𝗦

--
BACKGROUND

At the Village of Skokie Board of Trustees meeting on September 8, 2026 (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RjmNFg15eww), Trustee Alison Pure Slovin (District 2) told the Board that unlike her colleagues, several of whom described hearing concerns from residents about the Village's Flock automated license plate reader (ALPR) program, she had heard privately from constituents in her district who support the Flock cameras. In her words, as recorded in the meeting:

> "...we keep talking about the residents who've reached out to numerous trustees on this board. I'm concerned about these Flock cameras, as everybody said. But I can't speak for the other trustees. But I could tell you that people within the district that I serve, so to speak, have also reached out to me maybe privately and not to all the trustees and have said that they support it because they feel that there is a safety issue and anything that Skokie can do to keep them safe is something that they would commend us on and to continue with. So, you know, we're talking about the few that have reached out to us, but there are the others who are reaching out to us as well. And we have to balance both voices on this board as we move forward. And then if we talk about the amount of people who have reached out to us against Flock cameras, I can't speak for everybody else. It's a dozen people I've heard from. It's not like hundreds of people either. So, you know, we have to really look at who we're representing, what the needs are of this community, and how we help you keep them safe. And the recommendations are from the professionals, and I thank you for that."

Trustee Pure Slovin's comments came during the same September 8, 2026 meeting where the Skokie Police presented on its use of Flock Group ("Flock Safety") automated license plate readers (ALPR), and where numerous Skokie community members spoke during public comment against the Village's Flock ALPR camera network. 

Before public comment began, the board president instituted new decorum rules for the meeting, barring "clapping," "snapping," "standing," or "audible cheers," cast as necessary so that "all positions and voices can be expressed and heard without fear of reprisal." That public comment period then filled to its allotted capacity, roughly ten speakers at three minutes each, and with one exception unrelated to Flock (a labor dispute at a local bakery), every speaker who addressed the Village's Flock/ALPR program spoke against it. No speaker voiced support for Flock or ALPR on the record that night; the only support referenced anywhere in the meeting is the private, secondhand support Trustee Pure Slovin described above. Some quotes from that public comment period:

- "Flock is not an honest company," one commenter said, citing recent contract cancellations in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, and on state-run roads in Texas and Florida: "When I am on the same side as Ron DeSantis, I am embarrassed."
- Another commenter asked how the Village squares its own inclusion and belonging campaigns with "an atmosphere of distrust and fear that is created by flock cameras."
- A third commenter, working through a hypothetical involving a lawful firearm purchase, argued that Flock's camera network could function as a "de facto registry," with every Flock-equipped municipality along a driver's route adding to the trail.
- A commenter who worked through the Skokie Police Department's own case data noted that two of the resulting arrests were for cannabis in an improperly sealed container, not impaired driving, and asked whether those stops would have happened at all without "a false flag in the system."
- A commenter whose work involves information security argued "we can solve crimes without tracking everyone in public," and noted that Flock data collected in Skokie has already been reachable by outside agencies working around Illinois' restrictions on data sharing.
- A commenter affiliated with Lucy Parsons Labs and the Niles Coalition told the Board that the Skokie Police Department's Flock ALPR program has drawn scrutiny as part of "years of work by a coalition of researchers right here in Illinois," documented in a zine published at nilescoalition.org.
- A commenter warned that Flock's AI-enabled search tools mean "you don't really need facial recognition" to identify someone, since the system can be told to find a person matching a plain-language description and "bring in a live feed of that person as they're walking by."
- Another commenter said "there's just no reality on earth that comes to my mind that doesn't make this feel like an Orson Wells novel," adding that discussing "the idea of us living in a surveillance state" with the Board, over cameras that would also watch their own children, was hard to believe.
- A final commenter asked the Board directly how Flock can share footage with law enforcement on request when a homeowner's doorbell-camera network cannot do the same without a subpoena or the owner's consent.

The Lucy Parsons Labs/Niles Coalition commenter also said they had emailed the Board roughly six months earlier, in or around March 2026, with findings on the Skokie Police Department's use of ethnic slurs and its suppression of public ALPR audit logs, and that "nobody has followed up." That unanswered correspondence is part of why this request is being made: it, and any Trustee discussion or response it prompted, should fall within the scope of the records sought above.

During Board discussion of the Flock program, a Trustee referenced haveibeenflocked.com, a third-party tool that lets residents check whether their own license plate data has been captured by Flock cameras, as a resource that could help residents understand the program.

Skokie is one of many Chicago-area and Illinois municipalities where Flock automated license plate reader cameras (also called ALPR or license plate reader cameras) have become a point of public debate, alongside neighboring communities such as Evanston, Lincolnwood, Morton Grove, Wilmette, Winnetka, and Highland Park, and amid a broader statewide and national reckoning with the weapons technology tracked by organizations like Lucy Parsons Labs, the Niles Coalition, and the crowdsourced camera-mapping project DeFlock.org. The only reason Skokie PD, as with those across the country, started taking performative technological reforms was though diligent work by activists. That reckoning though has not slowed Skokie's own program: the Village's Flock cameras were already active by 2023 and remain in place through September 2026, notwithstanding the near-unanimous opposition voiced at the meeting described above. This request is part of an ongoing effort to obtain public records documenting how Flock Group ALPR surveillance technology is adopted and defended by outposts of empire like the Village of Skokie.

communications.subject: Extension Letter
communications.communication:
Dear Requester: 
  
 This email is in response to your recent request, Request Number: 1881-2026 made under the Freedom of Information Act. Section 3(e) of the Freedom of Information Act provides that the five-day response period may be extended for up to five additional working days for a limited number of reasons. Specifically: 
  
 Subsection 3(e)(i) states that the response time period may be extended if “the requested records are stored in whole or in part at other locations than the office having charge of the requested records” 
  
 Subsection 3(e)(ii) states that the response time period may be extended if “the request requires the collection of a substantial number of specified records”. 
  
 Subsection 3(e)(vii) states that the response time period may be extended if "there is a need for consultation, which shall be conducted with all practicable speed, with another public body or among 2 or more components of a public body having a substantial interest in the determination or in the subject matter of the request." 
  
 Pursuant to Subsections 3(e)(i), 3(e)(ii), and 3(e)(vii) we are notifying you of the Village’s intent to extend the time needed to research your request an additional five days. Your FOIA request will be completed no later than Friday, September 25. 
  
 Sincerely,

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: ILJAOC (CA) - PSDEX/AVCC Contributions and Data Sharing
communications.communication:
Hi Shawn,

This email will serve as the ILJAOC's preliminary response to your Public
Records Act request identified above. As you are aware, the CPRA generally
provides members of the public with the ability to request inspection or
copies of certain public records. However, an agency’s
obligation to make records available that are responsive to a request does
not require it
to create documents or to compile lists that otherwise do not exist.
Additionally, the
CPRA is not limitless and contains many exemptions from its disclosure
requirements.
In fact, there is no requirement to release an electronic record in its
original format if its
release could result in the disclosure of imbedded data that an agency has
a right, and
potentially a duty, to withhold.

Please note that while prompt access to public records is required by the
CPRA, the
CPRA provides the ILJ 10 days to provide an initial response to the
request. This
correspondence shall serve as the ILJ’s initial response and notification
that the ILJ will
require additional time to make this determination and hereby extends the
deadline to
produce any non-privileged or otherwise protected public records within 14
days of the
date of this letter, or June 15, 2026, as permitted by the CPRA.

To the extent the ILJ possesses responsive records, we will identify,
gather, and
redact such records to exclude all privileged information. The copies of
records responsive
to your request will be provided once the ILJ has had a reasonable time to
locate and review
these records, in PDF format.

If redaction requires preparing a printed copy, copies will be made
available to you
after you pay for the direct cost of duplication. The ILJ will notify you
of the anticipated
total cost for the copies of hard copy documents when all the documents are
compiled.

In the interim, it would help us to best focus the scope of the request if
you can clarify your question. When you ask "who contributes" do you mean
which agencies upload data that is visible to other agencies? And, when you
ask "who can access" do you mean which agencies can access the data of
other agencies? It would help in our search for a responsive document if
you could help clarify these questions. Thank you.

Please do not hesitate to contact me should you have any questions.

communications.communication:
Hi Kendra, 

Thank you for the detailed response. Based on our research, we have found that consortiums will sometimes restrict the data that participating agencies share to only be available to other consortium members. Other agencies and consortiums choose to contribute data to the national PSDEX pool - meaning their data is available to all AVCC customers. 

Who Contributes: We are trying to understand which ILJAOC members contribute data to a shared pool. Often times it's all agencies but we're seeking to understand if all ILJAOC members share data with one-another, or if some agencies chose not to share. We have found this is usually governed by a Data Sharing Agreement or MOU, or by the LexisNexis AVCC XML Addendum. 

Who Can Access: You are correct, we want to know which ILJAOC members can access data of other ILJAOC members. Is access to your data restricted to only other ILJAOC members (consortium private container), or is the data available to all AVCC subscribers in the national data pool via the Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEX)? 

I'm happy to answer more questions if it helps streamline your search or response. I appreciate it!

Best,
Shawn

title: Unredacted Production of Final Executed WSRMP Release of Claim / Settlement Contract (Shannon McMinimee — Case No. 18-2-09561-7)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Unredacted Production of Final Executed WSRMP Release of Claim / Settlement Contract (Shannon McMinimee — Case No. 18-2-09561-7)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The following single, distinct public record thoroughly identified and previously indexed by your office under closed Reference # P000166-040826:

RECORD REQUESTED: 

An unredacted or properly redacted copy of the final, signed, and executed Mutual Release Agreement / WSRMP Release of Claim Contract that officially concluded the litigation titled Shannon McMinimee v. Tacoma School District No. 10 (Pierce County Superior Court, Case No. 18-2-09561-7) in December 2018. This request explicitly targets the production of the 39 pages that were withheld in full on your June 18, 2026 Redaction Log.

PRE-EMPTIVE STATUTORY ENFORCEMENT & COMPLIANCE CLAUSE:The District is put on notice that its previous utilization of civil testimonial privilege statute RCW 5.60.060(2)(a) to execute a blanket 39-page blackout over a final executed contract is legally invalid under established Washington jurisprudence (Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co.). Civil testimonial rules do not constitute explicit PRA exemptions.

Furthermore, because final, executed settlement agreements funded by public risk pools are transactional business records as a matter of law (Yakima Newspapers v. City of Yakima), they cannot be withheld or redacted in full under the work-product doctrine (RCW 42.56.290).

To maximize administrative efficiency, the requester explicitly waives any interest in employee bank account numbers or routing metadata. The District is directed to apply a localized blackout exclusively to personal account strings, while releasing the formal contractual text, legal release conditions, and macro financial distributions disbursed on behalf of the taxpayers.

PRA STATUTORY DEADLINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a response is required within five (5) business days. Because this request targets one single, completed, pre-identified document already harvested by your office under Reference # P000166-040826, this should serve as a straightforward single-item pull to be delivered within your initial response window.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

It is my understanding that you are seeking the following records: "To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records: 

The following single, distinct public record thoroughly identified and previously indexed by your office under closed Reference # P000166-040826: 

RECORD REQUESTED: 

An unredacted or properly redacted copy of the final, signed, and executed Mutual Release Agreement / WSRMP Release of Claim Contract that officially concluded the litigation titled Shannon McMinimee v. Tacoma School District No. 10 (Pierce County Superior Court, Case No. 18-2-09561-7) in December 2018. This request explicitly targets the production of the 39 pages that were withheld in full on your June 18, 2026 Redaction Log. 

PRE-EMPTIVE STATUTORY ENFORCEMENT & COMPLIANCE CLAUSE:The District is put on notice that its previous utilization of civil testimonial privilege statute RCW 5.60.060(2)(a) to execute a blanket 39-page blackout over a final executed contract is legally invalid under established Washington jurisprudence (Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co.). Civil testimonial rules do not constitute explicit PRA exemptions. 

Furthermore, because final, executed settlement agreements funded by public risk pools are transactional business records as a matter of law (Yakima Newspapers v. City of Yakima), they cannot be withheld or redacted in full under the work-product doctrine (RCW 42.56.290). 

To maximize administrative efficiency, the requester explicitly waives any interest in employee bank account numbers or routing metadata. The District is directed to apply a localized blackout exclusively to personal account strings, while releasing the formal contractual text, legal release conditions, and macro financial distributions disbursed on behalf of the taxpayers. 

PRA STATUTORY DEADLINE: 

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a response is required within five (5) business days. Because this request targets one single, completed, pre-identified document already harvested by your office under Reference # P000166-040826, this should serve as a straightforward single-item pull to be delivered within your initial response window.

Sincerely, 

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #24-OIG-006
communications.communication:
U.S. Department of Justice
Office of Information Policy
FOIA Appeals
RE: Freedom of Information Act Appeal – Constructive Denial / Unreasonable Delay
Request No. 24-OIG-006
To Whom It May Concern:

I hereby appeal the failure of the Department of Justice Office of Inspector General (“OIG”) to provide a final determination regarding FOIA Request No. 24-OIG-006.

The request was acknowledged on October 6, 2023. The request concerns records relating to a DEA OPR investigation into the death of DEA Special Agent Jeffrey Bockelkamp.

More than one year later, on October 2, 2024, the OIG issued only an interim response stating that the records were still being processed and that the office was experiencing a backlog.

As of this appeal, the agency has exceeded the statutory response deadlines under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6). Generic assertions of backlog do not relieve the agency of its obligations under FOIA, particularly where the request is narrow in scope and seeks records of substantial public interest concerning the death of a federal law enforcement agent and the handling of any related investigation.

Accordingly, I request that the Office of Information Policy:

Conduct a de novo review of the handling of Request No. 24-OIG-006;

Direct the Office of Inspector General to immediately complete processing of the request;

Require the release of all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of responsive records;

Require the agency to provide a Vaughn index for any materials withheld in whole or in part;

Determine whether the prolonged delay constitutes improper withholding under FOIA.

To the extent responsive records originated with or were referred from the DEA, I further request confirmation regarding:

the volume of records referred;

the date(s) of referral;

whether consultations with other DOJ components remain pending; and

whether responsive records have already been identified and merely await disclosure review.

Because this request concerns government accountability and the handling of records relating to the death of a federal law enforcement agent, continued delay undermines the public’s ability to evaluate agency conduct and responsiveness.

I request electronic correspondence and production of records via email.
Sincerely,
/s/
William Fernandes

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #24-OIG-006
communications.communication:
Dear Office of Government Information Services:

I request OGIS assistance concerning DOJ Office of Inspector General FOIA/Privacy Act Request No. 24-OIG-006.

Agency: Department of Justice, Office of Inspector General
Request number: 24-OIG-006
Request subject: Records referred by the Drug Enforcement Administration concerning Jeffrey Bockelkamp
Response date: July 8, 2025

DEA referred 293 responsive pages to DOJ OIG. OIG’s response states that it reviewed all 293 pages, applied FOIA Exemptions 6, 7(C), 7(E), and 7(F), and enclosed the information that could be released.

However, OIG sent only a two-page response letter. The PDF contains no responsive records or other enclosure despite the letter expressly stating, “please find enclosed that information which can be released” and listing an “Enclosure.”

The response also does not identify:

* The number of pages released in full;
* The number released with redactions;
* The number withheld in full;
* Whether all 293 referred pages were accounted for; or
* Which exemptions correspond to the material withheld.

I have submitted an administrative appeal to DOJ’s Office of Information Policy requesting the missing enclosure, a complete page accounting, a renewed segregability review, and a sufficiently clear explanation of the disposition of all 293 pages.

I request OGIS assistance in communicating with DOJ OIG and determining:

1. Whether a release package was prepared but omitted from the transmission;

2. Whether OIG intended to withhold all 293 pages;

Subject: FOIA Administrative Appeal — DOJ OIG Request No. 24-OIG-006

Director
Office of Information Policy
U.S. Department of Justice

Dear Director:

I appeal the DOJ Office of Inspector General’s response to FOIA/Privacy Act Request No. 24-OIG-006 concerning records referred by the Drug Enforcement Administration regarding Jeffrey Bockelkamp.

OIG’s July 8, 2025 letter states that DEA referred 293 responsive pages, that OIG reviewed those 293 pages, and that “information which can be released” was enclosed. The letter also lists an “Enclosure.” However, the transmitted PDF contains only the two-page response letter. No responsive records or enclosure were provided.

The response is also materially unclear. It does not state:

1. How many of the 293 pages were released in full;

2. How many pages were released with redactions;

3. How many pages were withheld in full;

4. Whether all 293 referred pages were accounted for; or

5. Which pages or categories of information were withheld under Exemptions 6, 7(C), 7(E), and 7(F).

The statement that “certain portions” and unspecified “documents in their entirety” were excised does not provide a clear accounting of OIG’s disposition. Without the promised enclosure or a page-count breakdown, I cannot determine what was released, what was withheld, or meaningfully evaluate the asserted exemptions.

FOIA requires the release of all reasonably segregable nonexempt information. See 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A). DOJ regulations also treat the withholding of records in whole or in part as an appealable adverse determination. See 28 C.F.R. §§ 16.6 and 16.8.

I respectfully request that OIP:

1. Remand the request to OIG for immediate transmission of the missing enclosure and all records determined releasable;

2. Require OIG to provide a precise accounting of the 293 referred pages, identifying the number released in full, released in part, and withheld in full;

3. Require OIG to confirm that every referred page has been accounted for;

4. Require a sufficiently specific explanation of the exemptions applied to records withheld in full or in part; and

5. Require renewed segregability and foreseeable-harm reviews.

Although the response letter is dated July 8, 2025, OIP should accept this appeal because OIG never completed the stated production. The transmitted file contains no enclosure, and the response did not clearly disclose that no responsive pages had actually been provided. Alternatively, OIP should direct OIG to reissue a complete determination with the missing records and a new appeal period. [(Correspondence received 08/27/2026). False statements]

Please confirm receipt and assign an administrative appeal number.

Sincerely,

William Fernandes

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FBI JA 1.19.26
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:

You are receiving this correspondence as a request under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. subsection 552. I am requesting the following:

Copies of all Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) records, documents, and communications responsive to James Alexander Hamilton (June 9, 1907 — December 19, 1997; SSN 564-68-5620).

James Hamilton was a doctor of psychiatry at Stanford University who researched subjects ranging from alcoholism to post-partum depression between the 1940s and 1970s. While there, he also worked at the Vacaville California Medical Facility, using prisoners in medical studies that were later identified to have been covertly funded by the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). A reference to Dr. Hamilton's work can be found in a Los Angeles Times article about CIA-funded experiments published on January 30, 1979, available via the CIA's Reading Room: https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/docs/CIA-RDP88-01350R000200420014-3.pdf

Prior to his work for the CIA, Dr. Hamilton was a civilian employee of the Psychological Warfare Branch of the Military Intelligence Service and a commissioned officer in the Office of Strategic Services. One or both of these positions would have required the FBI to run a loyalty check, for security purposes. Dr. Hamilton was also a member of a World War II era truth drug committee created by the National Academy of the Sciences which the FBI participated in as an observer. A reference to the FBI's involvement with the committee can be found in a memo dated April 4, 1944, on page 59 of records related to bacteriological warfare it released to The Black Vault in 2005: https://www.theblackvault.com/documents/bacteriologicalwarfare.pdf

As such, I am requesting all FBI records responsive to Dr. James A. Hamilton.

Proof of death is not required as Dr. Hamilton's date of birth was over 100 years ago.

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Records System, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records related to all above referenced committees, agencies, and organizations.

I am asking you waive any fees associated with this request. I am a member of the news media. My bylines, which include Unicorn Riot, Covert Action Magazine, and the Geopolitical Economy Report, can be found in both print and electronic publications, and I am sending this request in coordination with Muckrock, an award-winning and nationally-recognized news organization. Please take note of the Office of Management and Budget guidelines published March 27, 1987 (52 FR 10012) that include electronic publications and other nontraditional publishers as representatives of the news media.

A fee waiver is appropriate in situations where "disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government, and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester,” 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(iii). As noted above, Dr. Hamilton worked for the Central Intelligence Agency on a covert basis conducting medical experiments on unwitting human subjects. This was covered extensively in the news in the 1970s, in the ensuing years in books like John Marks's The Search for the Manchurian Candidate and H. P. Albarelli Jr.'s A Terrible Mistake: The Murder of Frank Olson and the CIA's Secret Cold War Experiments, and more recently in television programs and online media. Any FBI records relevant to Dr. Hamilton would contribute significantly to public understanding of how the FBI vetted him, for what purposes this information may have been used by outside agencies, and the extent of his connections, overt or covert, to other government agencies.

In the event that there are fees, I am willing to pay up to $100. Please advise if fees will exceed this amount so I might make an arrangement for requesting the records. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

I look forward to your response within 20 working days, as the statute requires. If access to the records I am requesting will take longer, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

If you deny any or all of this request, please cite each specific exemption you feel justifies the refusal to release the information and notify me of the appeal procedures available to me under the law.

Sincerely,

Robert Skvarla, Jr.

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Flock Safety (South Fulton Police Department, South Fulton)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Public reports state that this town is using cameras from Flock Safety (a.k.a. "Flock"), the automatic license plate reader (ALPR) company. For the purposes of this request, when I refer to "Flock products," this includes hardware (Flock License Plate Readers (LPRs), Flock Safety Falcons, Flock Video Cameras, Flock Mobile Security Trailers, Flock Gunshot and Audio Detection Devices, Flock Drone as First Responder (DFRs), and Flock Alpha) as well as software (Flock Safety Platform, FlockOS, Flock911, Flock Nova, Flock FreeForm, Flock Vehicle Fingerprint technology, and the National LPR Network). Source: https://www.flocksafety.com/products

Therefore, pursuant to Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records (dated January 1, 2021 to the time this request is processed):

1. All contracts, purchase orders, invoices, receipts, payment records, budgetary quotes, and related procurement records involving Flock Safety.

2. All training, instructional, presentation, and guidance materials concerning the use of any Flock Safety product or service, including hardware and software. This includes, but is not limited to:
a) Presentations, videos, audio recordings, scripts, manuals, and training materials;
b) Meeting notes discussing the use of Flock products;
c) Technical or operational explanations of how Flock products function; and
d) Internal or external documents used to explain, train on, or promote the use of Flock products.

3. All policies, procedures, agreements, and legal documents relating to Flock Safety or its products, including terms and conditions, privacy impact assessments, standard operating procedures, use policies, data retention policies, legal opinions, warranties, nondisclosure agreements, memoranda of understanding, liability waivers, insurance agreements, and any other formal or informal agreements.

4. All audit, oversight, or compliance records relating to Flock Safety or its products, including security audits, misuse investigations, and reports submitted to oversight bodies.

5. All records reflecting requests from other law enforcement agencies or private entities for data obtained through Flock products, including but not limited to requests for LPR data.

6. All communications and documents that reference "Flock" / "Flock Safety," including emails, text messages, PDFs, word processing documents, spreadsheets, presentations, etc.

7. All communications with representatives of Flock Safety (email domain: @flocksafety.com)

Please try to include any other miscellaneous documents that facilitate this municipality's relationship with Flock that don't neatly fall neatly into the above categories.

I am a news reporter for WIRED (wired.com) so the requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. Therefore, I request that any fees are waived. But in the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available. I also respectfully ask that my request is expedited, given the newsworthiness of Flock and its activities.

If you need to contact me, you can reach me at caroline_haskins@wired.com, or here. Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,
Caroline Haskins

title: Public Records Request for Data on School Policing

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Public Records Request for Data on School Policing
communications.communication:
To whoever it may concern: 

This letter constitutes a request pursuant to the Public Records Act, G.L. c.66, §10, for public records in the custody of your school district. Under the Criminal Justice Reform Act,  school districts and law enforcement agencies must “specify the manner and division of responsibility for collecting and reporting the school-based arrests, citations and court referrals of students to the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education” (DESE).   DESE began collecting data on school-related arrests in the 2018-19 school year. In the 2019-20 school year, DESE has expanded that collection to include data on all referrals to law enforcement.  DESE has defined these terms as follows, borrowing the same definitions used by the U.S. Department of Education since its 2009 Civil Rights Data Collection.  

A school-related arrest “[r]efers to an arrest of a student for any activity conducted on school grounds, during off campus school activities (including while taking school transportation), or due to a referral by any school official. All school-related arrests are considered referrals to law enforcement.”  

A referral to law enforcement “[i]s an action by which a student is reported to any law enforcement agency or official, including a school police unit, for an incident that occurs on school grounds, during school-related events, or while taking school transportation, regardless of whether official action is taken. Citations, tickets, court referrals, and school-related arrests are considered referrals to law enforcement.”   


I request the following public records, as defined in G. L. c. 4, § 7 (twenty-sixth): 

1.	An extract of your records management system or database that includes each school-related arrest and each referral to law enforcement conducted during the 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, and 2021-2022 school year (up until the day the records are produced). Specifically, we request an extract of the database to include the following columns:
a.	Date of arrest or referral to law enforcement
b.	Time of arrest or referral to law enforcement
c.	Charge (or charges)
d.	Whether the individual(s) was arrested or referred to law enforcement
e.	Sex of individual(s) arrested or referred to law enforcement
f.	Age of individual(s) arrested or referred to law enforcement
g.	Race of individual(s) arrested or referred to law enforcement
h.	Ethnicity of individual(s) arrested or referred to law enforcement
i.	Disability status of the individual(s) arrested or referred to law enforcement
j.	Whether the individual arrested or referred to law enforcement is a student at the school.
k.	Name of arresting officer, if applicable, and 
l.	Badge number of the arresting officer or the officer that referred the youth to law enforcement, as applicable.

2.	If such an extract of the database in question 1 is not possible, please provide school incident reports on each school-related arrest and referral to law enforcement conducted during the 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, and 2021-2022 school year (up until the day the records are produced). 

3.	A copy of any active standard operating procedures developed with the police department and/or other law enforcement agencies regarding police placement or activity in your corresponding school;  and,

4.	Any records instructing or informing police personnel of, or otherwise describing data reporting requirements and procedures for complying with G.L. c. 71 § 37P(b).

5.	The cost to the school district of assigning a school resource officer to each school; and, 

6.	The total number of school resource officers and total number of guidance counselors for each school in your district for school years 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, and,

7.	The total number and a brief description of 911 calls from schools in your district to local police departments conducted during the 2018-2019, 2019-2020, 2020-2021, and 2021-2022, and, 

8.	A description of the proposed budget for mental, social, or emotional health support personnel for the school district.

As this request involves a matter of public interest and will not be used for any commercial purpose, we ask that all fees associated with this request be waived pursuant to 950 C.M.R. 32.07(2)(k). The purpose of this request is to determine whether your school district and police department are complying with their reporting obligations under the Criminal Justice Reform Act.  “The public has an interest in knowing whether public servants are carrying out their duties in an efficient and law-abiding manner.”    

It would be ill-advised to impose a fee for data that your school district may have failed to report in violation of statutory and regulatory duty.  Moreover, as you know, municipalities with a population of over 20,000 may not assess a fee for the first 2 hours of time spent searching for, compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested record. Finally, pursuant to 950 C.M.R. 32.07(2)(i), a records access officer shall assess no fee greater than the lowest hourly rate of a person capable of compiling, segregating, redacting and reproducing a requested record. In the event that a charge is incurred for this request which you will not waive, please so indicate and include an itemization of estimated good faith costs.
 
Please provide public records to a requestor in an electronic format unless the record is not available in an electronic format. G.L.c. 66, § 6A(d). 

The Public Records Act requires that you comply with this request within ten (10) business days following receipt. If you believe that documents or data responsive to any request herein is not public record and thus not subject to disclosure, please set forth in writing the specific reasons for such assertion, including the specific exemption or exemptions that you believe apply.  To the extent that you determine that records need to be redacted in order to be produced under any law protecting the privacy of named individuals, please do so rather than withholding them in their entirety.

If you have any questions about this request, or need additional time to respond, please contact me by phone at (617)-373-5862 or by email at k.stathulis@northeastern.edu. Thank you in advance for your prompt response to this request.
	
Sincerely, 


Katherine Stathulis, Esq.
Center for Public Interest, Advocacy, and Collaboration
Northeastern University School of Law
